agents.name: Claude Code

transport.quote: HTTP servers are the recommended option for connecting to remote MCP servers.

auth.quote: Some MCP servers don't support automatic OAuth setup via Dynamic Client Registration.

redirect_uri_form.quote: By default, Claude Code picks a random available port for the OAuth callback.

surfaces_prompts.quote: MCP servers can expose prompts that become available as commands in Claude Code.

agents.notes: Also discovers CIMD automatically; pre-registered --client-id/--client-secret and static headers are supported. Pre-registered redirect form: http://localhost:PORT/callback.

agents.name: Codex

transport.quote: Streamable HTTP servers: Servers that you access at an address.

auth.quote: OAuth authentication, including Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) and Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)

runs_where.quote: Local Codex clients can also connect directly to MCP servers and share their configuration.

agents.notes: CIMD and DCR both documented; login via `codex mcp login <server>`; static bearer_token_env_var / http_headers also supported. developers.openai.com/codex/mcp redirects here.

agents.name: Cursor

transport.quote: Cursor supports three transport methods: (table rows: stdio, SSE, Streamable HTTP)

auth.quote: With dynamic client registration, Cursor registers as a public client with no client secret.

redirect_uri_form.quote: Cursor uses fixed OAuth redirect URLs for MCP servers. (desktop: http://localhost:8787/callback)

surfaces_prompts.quote: Cursor supports these MCP protocol capabilities and extensions: (table row: Prompts, Supported)

runs_where.quote: Cloud Agents keep their own MCP sign-ins on Cursor's servers, separate from the sign-ins on your machine.

agents.notes: Desktop redirect http://localhost:8787/callback; web and Cloud Agents use hosted https://www.cursor.com/agents/mcp/oauth/callback. Quotes in parentheses summarise table rows on the page.

agents.name: Devin

transport.quote: HTTP (Streamable HTTP) is recommended for new integrations; SSE is supported for legacy servers.

auth.quote: For MCPs that authenticate with OAuth, Devin will prompt you to visit a URL to connect your account.

redirect_uri_form.quote: It is `https://api.devin.ai/mcp/oauth/callback` for every Devin deployment

agents.notes: Auth choices: None, Auth Header or OAuth; DCR named only for servers without it (own client id/secret).

agents.name: Droid

transport.quote: Droid supports three transports: **stdio** (local processes), **http** (Streamable HTTP, the current MCP standard, which streams responses over SSE internally), and **sse**

auth.quote: Droid discovers the authorization server, registers a client automatically via Dynamic Client Registration (DCR), and uses Factory's published client metadata when the server supports Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD).

redirect_uri_form.quote: Fixed localhost port for the OAuth callback (1-65535).

runs_where.quote: OAuth tokens are stored globally in your system keyring (or a fallback file)

agents.notes: Factory CLI. CIMD also supported; static --header and pre-registered oauth.clientId supported.

agents.name: GitHub Copilot

auth.quote: Static OAuth client ID (skips dynamic registration).

agents.notes: Surface documented: Copilot CLI. DCR is the default implied by the oauthClientId field description; client_credentials grant and static headers also supported. The Copilot cloud agent is reported not to support OAuth remote MCP servers (unverified).

agents.name: OpenCode

transport.quote: A remote server uses the MCP Streamable HTTP transport and requires an absolute URL:

auth.quote: With CIMD, OpenCode sends its metadata document URL as the client_id and skips registration:

redirect_uri_form.quote: Authorization servers accept any loopback port for these redirects, as RFC 8252 requires, so callback_port works with CIMD.

surfaces_prompts.quote: MCP prompts become commands named <server>:<prompt> with the same normalization.

runs_where.quote: When OpenCode runs over SSH, in a container, or on a remote server, the browser cannot reach OpenCode after you sign in

agents.notes: Order: pre-registered client, then CIMD, then DCR fallback. Static headers and oauth:false supported.

agents.name: Pi

transport.quote: Pi connects to Model Context Protocol servers over stdio or streamable HTTP and makes their tools and resources available to the model.

auth.quote: Without `clientId`, Pi identifies itself with its Client ID Metadata Document on pi.dev when the authorization server advertises support for documents and public clients. Otherwise it registers a client dynamically.

runs_where.quote: Pi reads user-level servers from `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` and project servers from `.pi/mcp.json`.

agents.notes: DCR fallback; legacy SSE not supported; static headers supported. Also at docs.pi.dev/latest/mcp.

agents.name: Vibe

transport.quote: `streamable-http` | The server is reachable over HTTP and supports streaming responses.

auth.quote: Without `client_id` or `client_metadata_url`, Vibe registers a client with the server dynamically.

redirect_uri_form.quote: After you approve access, the browser redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<redirect_port>/callback`

runs_where.quote: This address must reach the machine where Vibe runs.

agents.notes: Mistral Vibe CLI. CIMD via client_metadata_url when advertised; static auth supported.

agents.name: Visual Studio Code

transport.quote: `stdio` for a command, `http` for Streamable HTTP, or `sse` for a legacy SSE endpoint.

auth.quote: It also supports other OAuth identity providers through Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) or a pre-registered OAuth client.

redirect_uri_form.quote: Include `http://127.0.0.1:33418` and `https://vscode.dev/redirect` in the client's allowed redirect URLs.

surfaces_prompts.quote: The editor's `/mcp.<server>.<prompt>` picker and argument dialogs aren't exposed in Copilot sessions.

runs_where.quote: Local MCP servers can run code on your machine, and tools can access services using your permissions.

agents.notes: Both loopback http://127.0.0.1:33418 and hosted https://vscode.dev/redirect are used. Prompts are surfaced only in the deprecated Local harness.

agents.name: Command Code

transport.quote: Use `--transport http` to connect to remote MCP servers:

auth.quote: Command Code supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE for HTTP servers.

runs_where.quote: After you grant access, tokens are stored securely in ~/.commandcode/mcp-tokens.json.

agents.notes: Registration method not stated; optional pre-registered oauth.clientId and callbackPort; static headers supported.

agents.name: Bionic
agents.untested_reason: LM Studio's Bionic documentation does not cover MCP at all; only Cloudflare's page claims OAuth support
agents.notes: Classic LM Studio has MCP docs, but nothing says they apply to Bionic.
